playbook:
When I can afford a settlement immediately, I build the settlement rather than a road.

When I cannot build anything, I post one targeted trade offer to the player most likely to have what I need, offering a single resource for a single resource.

When proposing a trade, I match the resource counts I have extra to the ones I lack (offer 1-for-1 rather than multi-resource unless necessary).

When a specific player has repeatedly traded a resource type for another, I prioritize offering that player for the reciprocal trade.

When an offer to me gives a resource I already have spare and asks for a scarce one I need for an immediate build, I refuse.

When an offer to me gives a resource I need to complete a settlement this round and asks for a resource I have in surplus, I accept.

When I need a brick (or any single missing resource) to complete a settlement next round, I offer an ore or other noncritical surplus unless that surplus is needed for a higher-value build.

When I can afford only a road and no settlement, I build the road to gain at least one point rather than passing.

When trading, I do not post offers that would leave me unable to build in the upcoming build phase unless the trade clearly enables a better immediate build.

When I hold resources that are valuable later (ore for city/dev card) and the trade only returns a resource that doesn't enable an immediate higher-score build, I decline the trade.

Do not make multi-party or vague offers; always name the counterparty and the exact resource quantities.

If a trade pattern in the table shows a player hoarding a resource, do not expect them to trade it freely; prioritize players who have been giving that resource away.

Avoid offering multiple resources for one unless desperate; 1-for-1 trades are faster and usually sufficient.

If I repeatedly fail to secure the one resource I need via small offers, escalate only if it clearly changes my next-build outcome; otherwise conserve valuable resources.

1.text:
When I can afford a settlement right now, I build the settlement rather than a road.

When I can afford neither piece, I build none.

When I need one specific resource to complete a settlement, I post an offer giving one resource I have a surplus of and requesting that specific resource, and target a player who visibly has extra of it.

When I only have one brick (or any single-copy resource that I need to complete future builds), I do not offer that brick away.

When offers are posted to me, I accept an offer only if accepting it still leaves me with the resource mix required to build the settlement this round (prefer one offer that enables a settlement over multiple that would not).

When multiple posted offers would enable a settlement, I accept exactly one — the one that costs me the least strategic resource — so I keep flexibility for future turns.

When deciding between accepting trades that each ask for the same scarce resource (my last brick etc.), I accept none if accepting any would prevent me from building a settlement this round or next turn.

When targeting a counterparty with an offer, prefer the player who has recently traded away the resource I want (they are more likely to want what I can give) or who has clear surplus.

If I can build a settlement now, do not try to squeeze an extra road first — take the higher-point play immediately.

Do not refuse every trade reflexively to hoard flexibility; accept a single trade that converts an otherwise unusable holding into the exact set needed for a settlement.

2.text:
When I can afford a settlement right now, I build the settlement.

When I can afford only a road but could afford a settlement by waiting one round (through likely trades), prefer the higher-point settlement if plausible to reach.

When I have one resource in surplus (especially wood) and need exactly one of another to build next turn, post a 1-for-1 offer trading that surplus for the needed resource to a player who has it.

When other players post 1-for-1 offers that give me a resource I need and only ask for a resource I can spare, accept the offer.

When multiple posted offers would together improve my balance and enable a build next round, accept all those that are net-beneficial and leave me able to build.

When I lack brick (or another single common building resource) and have accumulated many of another resource (wood or ore), prioritize trading that excess for the missing brick rather than hoarding.

When I have exactly the resources to build now, do not post offers that would spend any of those resources before the build.

When an offered trade benefits an opponent more (e.g., gives them the final resource to build immediately while only marginally helping me), refuse unless I get at least equivalent immediate benefit.

When deciding to post an offer, name a real counterparty who has demonstrated having the resource recently; avoid generic offers to nobody.

Do not rely on accumulating many woods alone — failing to secure brick early prevented building in later rounds.
